messages:
sam_support: FYI customer acme-corp opened SUP-4821 — sudden p95/p99 latency jump on /v1/generate since ~09:10 UTC. They see auth handshakes timing out then retries hit high latency.

sam_support: Quick summary: p50 stable, p95 up from 120ms -> 380ms, p99 up to 1.6s for small prompts (<32 tokens). Error rate small but latency spike impacts interactive UI.

sam_support: Observed during rollout window: yesterday at 22:00 we pushed continuous-batcher default tweaks (hold_window increased to 30ms globally to improve throughput). Suspect tiny requests being held waiting for batch size and auth handshake overlap.

jess_cust: confirming — our UI started timing out users at ~09:15. We see a few 401 retries then long tails. Happy to coordinate for repro.

olivia_sre: thx. can you drop a quick p95/p99 graph link? also need logs for the auth failure path (X-Request-ID) from their traces.

sam_support: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/latency/acme-corp?from=6311122000&to=6311122600 — shortlink in thread. Attached two example Request-IDs: req_8f3a, req_8f7c.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-112 created and assigned to olivia_sre.

olivia_sre: grabbing traces now. initial look: a lot of requests showing hold_window waiting time of ~28-32ms before batching. After hold expires they kick, then auth handshake (tenant token fetch) adds 40–120ms. Tiny prompt path therefore hits p99.

olivia_sre: hypothesis: increasing hold_window reduced CPU overhead on busy GPUs but for tenants with many tiny interactive requests it increases tail due to auth knob interactions.

kai_platform: we saw this pattern in canary last month with coalesce+auth sync. options: 1) reduce hold_window for affected tenant 2) enable per-tenant bypass for <64 token flows 3) quick rollback of global change.

sam_support: customer is preferring a fast mitigation vs rollback. they can tolerate small throughput delta.

maya_oncall: propose temporary config patch: set batching.hold_window=5ms for tenant acme-corp and enable early-emit for tiny payloads. I'll run canary to 5% then 50% if green.

olivia_sre: sounds good. runbook steps:
1) rwdctl feature set batching.hold_window --tenant=acme-corp --value=5ms --env=prod
2) rwdctl feature set batching.early_emit_threshold --tenant=acme-corp --value=64 --env=prod
3) watch p95/p99 and auth error rate for 15m

sam_support: adding exact commands — using console API token: 

```
# set hold window to 5ms for the tenant
rwdctl tenant-config patch acme-corp --set "batching.hold_window=5ms" --env prod
# set early emit for tiny prompts
rwdctl tenant-config patch acme-corp --set "batching.early_emit_threshold=64" --env prod
```

kai_platform: also add a short-circuit for token fetch: enable token-cache-ttl=30s for acme-corp to reduce auth roundtrip variance. command: `rwdctl tenant-config patch acme-corp --set "auth.token_cache_ttl=30s"`

jess_cust: we can do token cache change on our side too if needed. but prefer if you do tenant-side change first.

maya_oncall: patch applied to 5% (canary) at 09:48 UTC. monitoring now.

olivia_sre: initial 5m check: p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 380ms in canary hosts. auth error count unchanged (small), auth latency tail improved slightly.

maya_oncall: increasing canary to 50% at 09:58. will watch for errors.

opsbot: Change ticket CHG-7591 updated: hold_window override + early_emit + token_cache_ttl.

sam_support: customer notified, they see improvement in staging and are re-testing prod flows.

olivia_sre: followup notes: we should avoid global large hold_window for now. Add a rule to default to smaller hold for tenants with median prompt length < 64 tokens or high auth-roundtrips. Filed RFC: PLT-186 to make per-tenant adaptive hold_window.

kai_platform: short-term mitigation added to config service: a per-tenant "tinyflow" opt-in that disables coalescing for <64 token requests. Will scope rollout after postmortem.

sam_support: customer confirms UX now responsive. Marking SUP-4821 as "mitigated" pending postmortem items.

maya_oncall: closing canary at 10:20 after 22m at 50%. p95 back to baseline (~110ms), p99 ~400ms. will keep the tenant override for 24h then reassess.

jess_cust: thanks team, appreciate the fast fix.

olivia_sre: owners: olivia_sre (investigation), kai_platform (config change), maya_oncall (deployment), sam_support (customer comms). Postmortem owner: olivia_sre.

sam_support: next steps: add regression alert for hold_window changes that increases p99 for tiny prompts by >50% (SUP-4821 follow-up).

olivia_sre: saved logs and traces under /incidents/INC-2026-112/traces and will draft postmortem. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
